texts.facts: The plaintiff in Com. O.S No.253/2024 on the file of the XI Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru Rural District, (henceforth referred to as 'the Commercial Court') has filed this petition challenging an order dated 17.09.2024 by which the Commercial Court issued emergent notice on the interlocutory applications i.e., I.A Nos.II and III and suit summons to defendant Nos.1 and 2 and refused to grant ex parte interim injunction. 2. The suit in Com.O.S No.253/2024 was filed for perpetual injunction to restrain the defendants from manufacturing, labelling and selling products under the brand name "SANGAVI FOODS". He also sought for mandatory injunction to direct the defendant No.1 to get transferred the food licence issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ('FSSAI' in short) to the business conducted by the plaintiff. He sought for perpetual injunction to restrain the defendants from interfering with his running of the business NC: 2024:KHC:41724 and from interfering with his possession of the factory established in the suit schedule properties. 3. The plaintiff claimed that he is the son of the defendant No.1 who established a factory named 'SANGAVI FOODS'. The defendant No.1 had obtained a licence from FSSAI to manufacture food products. The defendant No.1 and his son - Sri R Lokesh executed a memorandum of understanding in favour of the plaintiff on 01.10.2022 in terms of which the defendant No.1 offered to the plaintiff to take over the business of 'SANGAVI FOODS'. The plaintiff had agreed to pay Rs.3,15,000/- every month towards repayment of loan to M/s.Hinduja Finance. He also agreed to pay Rs.50,000/- to the defendant No.1 for his maintenance and Rs.25,000/- for the maintenance of his elder brother. The plaintiff claimed that he was placed in possession of the factory and that he was running it. He claimed that the factory was established on the suit 'A' and 'B' schedule properties. The suit 'A' schedule property was purchased in the name of the mother of the plaintiff while the suit 'B' schedule property was purchased in the name of the defendant No.1. The agreement dated 01.10.2022 was to be in force for a period of three years and could be terminated after NC: 2024:KHC:41724 issuing a nine months prior notice. The plaintiff claimed that due to disputes Sri Kiran Kumar R vs Sri Raju Kadegowda on 15 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146703325/ 2 between the plaintiff and defendant No.1, the latter issued a notice dated 24.05.2024 terminating the agreement dated 01.10.2022. The attempts of the plaintiff to resolve the dispute failed. The defendant No.1 issued another notice dated 26.06.2024 calling upon the plaintiff to hand over the possession of the unit and the business with accounts. The plaintiff claims that he came to know that the defendant No.1 was running a factory in the name and style - M/s.Samrat foods to manufacture and sell products under the brand name 'SANGAVI FOODS', illegally. The plaintiff therefore lodged a complaint with the Police which resulted in Crime No.554/2024. The defendant No.1 filed a suit in O.S. No.382/2024 on the file of III Additional Civil Judge and JMFC., Nelamangala for perpetual injunction in respect of the suit 'A' schedule property. Following this, he got the address mentioned in FSSAI licence transferred to the address of the defendant No.2. The plaintiff therefore, claimed that the defendants were likely to interfere with his business and hence sought the aforementioned reliefs. Applications for interim injunction were filed which were numbered as I.A. Nos.II and III. I.A. No.II was filed for NC: 2024:KHC:41724 injunction to restrain the defendants from manufacturing and labelling products under the name 'SANGAVI FOODS' while I.A. No.III was filed for interim injunction to restrain the defendant No.1 from interfering with the business and management of 'SANGAVI FOODS' established in the suit schedule properties pending disposal of the suit. The Commercial Court after considering the said applications, issued emergent notice on I.A. Nos.II and III and suit summons to the defendants and did not grant ex parte injunction that was prayed by the plaintiff. 4. Being aggrieved by the same, the plaintiff is before this Court.
texts.arguments: 5. Learned counsel for the plaintiff vehemently contended that when once the business was handed over to the plaintiff under an agreement dated 01.10.2022, the defendant No.1 could not have indulged in any act to commit the breach of the agreement. He, therefore, contended that the Commercial Court ought to have granted ex parte interim injunction orders to ensure that the agreement dated 01.10.2022 is not breached. Besides this, he contended that the Commercial Court did not apply its mind to the facts and NC: 2024:KHC:41724 circumstances of the case before holding that the plaintiff had not made out a prima facie case for grant of ex parte injunction. The impugned order discloses that the Commercial Court had perused the averments made in the plaint and had also looked into the apprehension of the NC: 2024:KHC:41724 plaintiff and held that the defendant No.1 had obtained an ex parte interim order of injunction in O.S. No.382/2024 in respect of the suit 'A' schedule property and therefore, it felt inappropriate to grant an ex parte order of injunction in respect of the Sri Kiran Kumar R vs Sri Raju Kadegowda on 15 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146703325/ 3 suit schedule properties.
